name: Waldorf Astoria Panama
positioning: City hotel near Calle Uruguay and the Cinta Costera, opened in 2013 as the first Waldorf in Latin America
best_for: Travelers who want a central Panama City base near the waterfront and the financial district
Guests who enjoy cocktail bars, afternoon tea and terrace dining
Families who want cribs, childcare and longer-stay suites with kitchens

facts.text: The hotel is one block from the Cinta Costera and close to the financial district.
The hotel is surrounded by the nightlife of Calle Uruguay and is minutes from Casco Viejo.
Rooms and suites have city or ocean views.
Rooms have Sodashi amenities in the marble bathroom.
The studio suite offers Panama Bay and Pacific Ocean views and a full-size kitchen.
Matiz serves a blend of international and Panamanian cuisine on the terrace.
At dinner, chefs at Matiz prepare steaks, seafood and pasta in the open kitchen.
The Bungalow is an indoor-outdoor lounge serving light meals, smoothies and cocktails.
Peacock Alley hosts an afternoon tea service with tea or coffee, sweet and savory pastries and a mimosa.
Spa therapists use local ingredients in every treatment.
The hotel offers cribs and childcare.
A kosher box breakfast is available, endorsed by Vaadat Hakashrut Shevet Ahim.

highlights.text: The hotel opened in 2013 as the first Waldorf in Latin America.
The hotel has a personal concierge certified by Les Clefs d'Or.
The outdoor pool is on the seventh floor, with views of Panama City.
Peacock Alley, the hotel's cocktail bar, serves sipping liquors, aged rum and single-malt scotch.
In the Le Petit Chef dining experience, the table transforms into an immersive 3D stage.

considerations.text: This is a hotel in the heart of the city, near Calle Uruguay; its outdoor pool is on the seventh floor.
WhataHotel notes ultra-luxury pricing that may not suit all budgets.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Waldorf Astoria Panama
